fluff.overview:
The Panther was originally conceived as a fire-support vehicle for reconnaissance units during the waning years of the Star League. Commissioned in 2739, Alshain Weapons began delivering the first Panthers to the SLDF for operations against renegade bandits along the Periphery borders. The original PNT-8Z model's poor performance at the Battle of St. John in 2759 revealed critical flaws in its main weapon, prompting Star League engineers to replace the troublesome Tronel large laser with the Lord's Light PPC.

This revision established the PNT-9R as the preeminent light BattleMech design for the Draconis Combine throughout the Succession Wars. The Combine remains the only Successor State to field the Panther in significant numbers, with the design becoming as iconic to the DCMS as the Dragon or Atlas. Its combination of heavy firepower and jump capability has made it a cornerstone of Combine doctrine for over three centuries.
fluff.capabilities:
The Panther's primary armament is a Lord's Light PPC mounted in the right arm, providing firepower unusual for a 'Mech of its tonnage. The Lord's Light combines the damage output of a standard particle cannon with the lightness of an arm-carried weapon, though the design's thirteen single heat sinks struggle to dissipate the weapon's considerable waste heat. Many DCMS officers view this as an advantage, using the Panther as a training platform where recruits learn heat management before advancing to heavier designs.

The PPC is supplemented by a Telos Four-Shot SRM-4 launcher mounted in the center torso, providing close-range punch when enemies close to point-blank range. Four Lexington Lifter jump jets grant a 120-meter jumping distance, enabling the mobility necessary for its fire-support role. Six and a half tons of Maximillian armor provide respectable protection, though pilots know better than to engage heavier opponents in sustained firefights.

Star League pilots discovered that the Panther excels at urban combat, earning it the nickname "Alley Cat" from Lyran MechWarriors. Its jump capability navigates restricted city spaces while its PPC can disable heavy opponents from rooftop sniping positions.
fluff.history:
The Draconis Combine inherited Alshain Weapons' Panther factories when the Star League dissolved, quickly putting the production lines to work building Panthers for the DCMS. The design saw its first large-scale Combine deployment during the First Succession War when the Twenty-Third Galedon Regulars used their Panthers to maul the heavier 'Mechs of the Forty-Second Avalon Hussars at New Mendham, establishing the tactical doctrine that would define Panther operations for centuries.

Throughout the Succession Wars, the Combine was the only significant user of the Panther, often pairing it with the Jenner in a deadly combination of speed and firepower. Panthers provided covering fire while faster Jenners flanked opponents, a tactic that proved devastatingly effective against slower formations. Other Successor States employed Panthers in smaller numbers, typically older League-era 8Z models obtained through battlefield salvage, though replacement parts remained scarce outside Combine space.

Demand for the Panther forced Alshain Weapons to open a secondary facility on Jarett, but both factories were eventually lost. New Oslo transferred to the Free Rasalhague Republic following its formation in 3034, where the Panther quickly became a mainstay of the Royal KungsArmé. During the Clan Invasion, both Alshain and New Oslo fell to Clan Ghost Bear while a Free Rasalhague Republic plant on Satalice was captured by Clan Wolf.

Alshain Weapons crash-built a new facility on Tok Do in 3053, but could not maintain pre-invasion production levels and focused on spare parts and upgrade kits instead. Wakazashi Enterprises eventually purchased the Panther production license, answering Kanrei Minamoto's call for industrial diversification, and began rolling out new variants from New Samarkand. The PNT-10K quickly replaced the venerable 9R as the most common model in DCMS service, seeing action throughout the Jihad and into the Dark Age era.
fluff.deployment: An extensive upgrade designed to address the 10K's heat management issues while maintaining combat effectiveness. The ER PPC was replaced with an ER large laser and medium pulse laser combination, while the SRM-4 launcher was upgraded to a Streak model for improved accuracy. A targeting computer enhances accuracy across all weapons systems, and the single heat sinks were replaced with ten double-strength models. Additional armor provides improved survivability. Prestigious units such as the Genyosha and Sword of Light brigades utilize the more heat-efficient 12A variant.
